r.지역: Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan
r.문화권·종교: Dari and Pashto · mostly Sunni Muslim
r.경제 체제: Farm economy cut off from aid under Taliban rule · minerals undeveloped
r.한국이 파는 것: Beverages 32%, Cars 23%, Refined petroleum 6%, Vaccines, blood products 6% (2025, share of value)
r.한국이 사는 것: Salt, stone, minerals 79%, Ores 16%, Sneakers and footwear 1% (2025, share of value)
r.정치 구도: As US troops withdrew in August 2021, the Taliban took Kabul and declared an 'Islamic Emirate'. There is no constitution and no elections: a supreme leader based in Kandahar in the south rules by religious decree, and the cabinet in Kabul carries out his will. Girls cannot attend school beyond primary level or go to university, and women are barred from many jobs and even from parks. In 2024 a law went further, restricting women's voices and clothing in public. Other countries say ties can only deepen if the ban on women's education is lifted, but the Taliban call it an internal matter and refuse to budge.

t.why: A landlocked crossroads linking Central Asia, South Asia and Iran, it has long been a battleground for great powers. The 1979 Soviet invasion and the 2001 US-led invasion brought more than 40 years of war. Almost no country formally recognizes the Taliban government, though Russia became the first to do so in 2025. Pakistan accuses Afghanistan of sheltering the Pakistani Taliban who attack it, and since 2025 it has carried out airstrikes and border clashes, with ceasefires and talks repeatedly breaking down. In 2025 alone about 2.8 million Afghans returned or were expelled from Iran and Pakistan, deepening the humanitarian crisis.
t.rel: After the Taliban returned to power in 2021, almost no country formally recognized the government until Russia did so first in 2025. It clashes often with Pakistan over militants on the border and has water and refugee issues with Iran.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in 1973, broken off after the communist coup of 1978 and restored in 2002. From 2002 to 2007 South Korea stationed the Dongui medical unit and the Dasan engineering unit at Bagram Air Base. In 2007 the Taliban kidnapped 23 Korean volunteers and killed two of them, and from 2010 to 2014 South Korea ran a Provincial Reconstruction Team in Parwan province that built a hospital and a vocational training center. Right after the Taliban takeover in 2021 it closed its embassy and brought about 390 Afghans who had worked for the embassy and its aid projects, along with their families, to Korea as 'special contributors'.
t.know: Two giant Buddhas in the Bamiyan Valley were blown up by the Taliban in 2001; only the empty niches remain.
etext: Most people live off farming and herding, growing wheat, fruit and nuts. Before the Taliban took power, foreign aid covered a large part of the state budget; afterwards aid fell sharply and central bank assets held abroad were frozen.
The Taliban banned poppy growing in 2022, and the area under cultivation fell 95% the following year. Farmers lost the income poppies brought, but replacement crops and jobs are still scarce.

It is believed to hold large deposits of copper, iron ore and lithium. A Chinese company won the rights to develop the Mes Aynak copper mine in the late 2000s, but security and infrastructure problems kept the project stalled for years.

As a landlocked country it depends on ports in Pakistan and Iran for its trade. When borders close, trade stops, and the influx of people returning from neighboring countries has left jobs and food in short supply.
